variables.title: Variables
variables.notes: Same as Prolog, uppercase letters denote variables.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Adapted: Encapsulated objects and protocols act as types.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
loop(0).
loop(N) :-
    N > 0,
    N2 is N - 1,
    loop(N2).
while_loop.notes: Adapted: Recursion is used for loops.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
:- public(add/3).
add(A, B, C) :- C is A + B.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Standard Prolog catch mechanism for message sending.

comments.title: Comments
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment in Logtalk
/* Multi-line comment */
comments.notes: Logtalk uses -- for line comments and /* */ for blocks.

numbers.title: Numbers & Decimal Data
numbers.notes: Logtalk represents exact decimal precisions alongside standard integer types.

booleans.title: Booleans & Predicates
booleans.code:
-- Three-valued logic (TRUE, FALSE, UNKNOWN)
WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND deleted_at IS NULL
booleans.notes: Logtalk evaluates predicates using declarative boolean conditions with NULL semantics.

type_casting.title: Type Casting (CAST/CONVERT)
type_casting.notes: Logtalk casts types using CAST(expr AS target_type) expressions.

strings.title: Strings & Text Literals
strings.code: SELECT 'String literal' AS col, N'Unicode text' AS unicode_col;
strings.notes: Logtalk encloses character literals in single quotes with optional N prefix for Unicode.

string_formatting.title: String Concatenation
string_formatting.code: SELECT CONCAT('User: ', username, ' (', email, ')') FROM users;
string_formatting.notes: Logtalk formats and joins textual columns using CONCAT or string concatenation operators.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching (LIKE & CASE)
pattern_matching.code:
SELECT CASE 
    WHEN score >= 90 THEN 'A'
    WHEN score >= 80 THEN 'B'
    ELSE 'C'
END AS grade
WHERE email LIKE '%@example.com';
pattern_matching.notes: Logtalk performs conditional classification via CASE WHEN and pattern search with LIKE.

range.title: Ranges (BETWEEN & LIMIT/OFFSET)
range.notes: Logtalk defines range intervals with BETWEEN and pagination ranges via LIMIT/OFFSET.

iterators.title: Cursors & Window Functions
iterators.notes: Logtalk processes ordered sequences set-by-set using window functions or procedural cursors.

oop_classes.title: Schemas & Tables (Entities)
oop_classes.notes: Logtalk structures entities through relational tables, constraints, and views.

lists.title: Tables & Arrays
lists.code:
-- Array or temporary result table
SELECT ARRAY[1, 2, 3] AS num_list;
lists.notes: Logtalk supports array column types or relation rowsets representing lists.

tuples.title: Rows & Composite Types
tuples.notes: Logtalk represents tuples as table rows or composite record types.

sets.title: Set Queries (UNION, INTERSECT)
sets.notes: Logtalk combines dataset results using relational algebra (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT).

modules_import.title: Schemas & Extensions
modules_import.code:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS "uuid-ossp";
SET search_path TO my_schema, public;
modules_import.notes: Logtalk manages namespaces and modular capabilities through schemas and extensions.
